item.text: {"question_id":"3B.2","answer":"For 2023, Tshisekedi had formal authority over national coercive institutions and made relevant appointments, including Jean-Pierre Bemba as defense minister and Peter Kazadi as interior minister; he also addressed the FARDC as commander-in-chief, directing it to defend institutions and the population and promising government support (BATCH-0009-E003; BATCH-0019-E010). The government reported commander commitments, an FARDC ethics and conduct code, military and judicial training, police-investigation capacity building, inspections, joint patrols, and an inquiry into alleged FARDC violence (BATCH-0011-E004; BATCH-0009-E005; BATCH-0011-E003). These establish appointments, directives, and institutional activity, but not adequate resourcing, implementation, effective discipline, or nationwide outcomes; several claims are self-reported or partner-supported and the reported reduction in FARDC sexual violence is not independently quantified. Contrary evidence is materially stronger on operational control and discipline: at least 12 FARDC soldiers arrested and beat three journalists, with no documented accountability outcome (BATCH-0026-E007); surrendered Mobondo fighters were sent to military training without vetting for prior abuses, and at least 80 civilians were reportedly killed by Congolese security forces within a larger 2023 civilian death toll (BATCH-0010-E015). The administration also supported Wazalendo and FDLR forces alongside Congolese troops and contracted private military personnel, creating aligned-actor accountability risks (BATCH-0028-E016). In Goma, national security forces carried out a planned operation that killed at least 56 people according to the official count, injured more than 80, and arbitrarily arrested more than 150; some security personnel were convicted, but investigations and proceedings were materially incomplete and flawed (BATCH-0011-E018; BATCH-0011-E021). The documented orders, knowledge, and alleged failure to prevent or punish concern provincial commander Constant Ndima, not a proven personal presidential order or approval by Tshisekedi (BATCH-0011-E022). Overall, formal authority and some preventive or corrective measures coexisted with recurring failures to vet, prevent, investigate, and discipline coercive forces and aligned actors; the evidence supports national-policy and appointment attribution more strongly than attribution for individual provincial or unit
